title: `for…of` over a foreign value calls its `Symbol.iterator`, so the loop is a foreign call and the enclosing row keeps the panic case
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." A `for…of` head is such a call: the language invokes `iterable[Symbol.iterator]()` and then `next()` on whatever that returns, and both are members the foreign module supplies. There is no call expression to lower, which is exactly why this was fail-open — the machinery was keyed on `ts.CallExpression`/`ts.NewExpression`, so `main` compiled with a row reading `failures: []` while the foreign iterator threw straight out of it. poc/src/language/README.md registers the closure under `SMITHERS1506` as ONE predicate over an expression's position (`implicitInvocationProtocol`) rather than a list of reporting sites.
